chunks: And hold fast to the Book of Allah, for it is the strong rope of Allah, the clear path, the call, and the remembrance. He who clings to it will not go astray, and he who holds onto it will not perish.

And hold fast to the Sunnah of his Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and the family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), for they will not separate until they reach the Pool (al-Kawthar) for you.
And hold fast to the Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), for they are the life of knowledge and the death of ignorance.
They are the ones whose rulings inform you of their knowledge, their silence informs you of their speech, and their outward appearance informs you of their inner self.
They do not contradict the religion, nor do they differ within it regarding it; so it is among them a truthful witness and a silent speaker.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِ النَّبِيِّ: The Family of the Prophet, specifically referring to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.السُّنَّة: The Sunnah, the tradition/practice of the Prophet
key_terms.الْحَوْض: The Pool (of Kawthar), a sign of intercession on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.حَبْلُ اللَّهِ: The Rope of Allah, a metaphor for the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Ahl al-Bayt in relation to the Quran and Sunnah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali establishes the Ahl al-Bayt as the hermeneutical key to the Quran, arguing that true understanding of divine law requires knowing those who preserved its essence against alteration. This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine of the Infallibles as the living embodiment of the Book, where their silence and speech serve as authoritative interpretations of the text's apparent and hidden meanings. It positions them not merely as transmitters, but as the definitive standard by which the integrity of the religion is measured.

en.sayed-ali-raza: You should know that you will never know guidance unless you know who has abandoned it, you will never abide by the pledges of the Qur’ān unless you know who has broken them, and will never cling to it unless you know who has forsaken it.
Seek these things from those who own them because they are the life spring of knowledge and death of ignorance.

They are the people whose commands will disclose to you their (extent of) knowledge, their silence will disclose their (capacity of) speaking and their outer appearance will disclose their inner self.
They do not go against religion, and do not differ from one another about it, while it is among them a truthful witness and a silent speaker.
